LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.2 PRONUNCIATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Pronunciation, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What can we do to ensure that we stress correctly? 2. Why should we pronounce sounds accurately?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. say sentences featuring words with variant stress, for example, con.vict (n) con.vict (v. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication,

2. listen to a list of words such as: rebel(noun) –rebel(verb) Produce(noun)- produce(verb) 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say sentences featuring words with variant stress, for example, con.vict (n) con.vict (v. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication,
2. listen to a list of words such as: rebel(noun) –rebel(verb) Produce(noun)- produce(verb) 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy as learner applies their digital skills as they listen to a recording of disyllabic words whose stress is on the

second syllable for both nouns and verbs.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as learner portrays patience as they play sounds games such as “silently mouthing” or “tell me when I

am odd” and record themselves using digital devices.

Life skills and social awareness: The learners exercise empathy as they exchange words and give feedback on their
